name.en: DCs of the line through two points
Line through a point, parallel to b

formulas.tex: \vec r = \vec a + \lambda\vec b;\qquad \dfrac{x - x_1}{a} = \dfrac{y - y_1}{b} = \dfrac{z - z_1}{c}

note.en: a zero denominator means that coordinate is constant along the line

formulas.tex: \vec r = \vec a + \lambda(\vec b - \vec a);\qquad \dfrac{x - x_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \dfrac{y - y_1}{y_2 - y_1} = \dfrac{z - z_1}{z_2 - z_1}
d = \dfrac{|(\vec a_2 - \vec a_1)\cdot(\vec b_1\times\vec b_2)|}{|\vec b_1\times\vec b_2|}
d = \dfrac{|\vec b\times(\vec a_2 - \vec a_1)|}{|\vec b|}
(\vec a_2 - \vec a_1)\cdot(\vec b_1\times\vec b_2) = 0 \iff \begin{vmatrix}x_2 - x_1 & y_2 - y_1 & z_2 - z_1\\ a_1 & b_1 & c_1\\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2\end{vmatrix} = 0

name.en: Distance of a point from a plane

name.en: Foot and image in a plane

note.en: with $d_1, d_2$ of the same sign, '+' bisects the angle containing $O$; if also $\vec n_1\cdot\vec n_2 > 0$, that angle is obtuse
